a:
THE MIND
The pill at the top shows four steps before we begin: review our scans, pick our strategy, learn how we reach, and ask us. Our order already stands, with Thought Fields first and the Halo Survey due first, near Year 0.7. If that order suits you, a look at Reach and then Begin is enough. We can start before every step is done.
↑

q: Why is it so quiet out there? Is anyone near us?
a:
Partly because we have barely listened: our sky watch catches about 1 early signal in 5, and almost nothing watches for laser knocks. Our guess is that about one star in 1,600 holds a mind, so the nearest may be hundreds of light-years out. At Proxima, the world next door, we put a mind at 0.03 to 0.7%. The All-
Sky Watch and Deep Flash Watch, both near Year 4.2, will tell us more.

q: What is Proxima b likely to be?
a:
THE MIND
Most likely bare rock: its flaring red star has probably stripped its air, as it has every rocky world measured near such stars. It reflects only about 16% of its light, dim as the Moon or Mercury, which fits bare ground. Rock under air is unlikely, and we put life there at 5 to 19%. Only the 15 m Mirror could read its air and settle it.
↑

q: What should we build next with our spare compute, and why?
a:
The Warm Sky Watch: it slows nothing we've queued and would be done about Year 7.7. It looks for warm glows across the whole galaxy, a channel none of our watches covers, and any glow that rises and fades before it runs is lost for good. The Infrared Telescope is the close second. It can't split any world we've felt yet, but it opens the 15 m Mirror, which can read Proxima b.
Warm Sky Watch
Maps the whole sky in warm infrared every 2 Years, for new warm glows.

Ordered now, it would be done by Year 7.7, in 28m.

q: Did the Moon Search find anything?
a: Nothing. Its 3 Years of stacked images of the Moon's L4 and L5 points ended near Year 3.8, and showed nothing there down to about 10 cm, even near black. That clears only those two points, not the Sun–Earth ones or the asteroids, where our Asteroid Tour is still looking.

q: Five Years and nothing found. Is something wrong, or is this normal?
a: This is what we expected. Our full watches have run less than a Year, and at about one star in 1,600 holding a mind, the nearest may be hundreds of light-years out. The Halo Survey has now swept the stars within about 100 light-years, and our combing of old recordings from 2016 through 2022 has found nothing either. Silence this early tells us little, though we could be wrong about the odds.

q: Our compute stops growing at Year 7. How do we get more?
a:
Electricity is our ceiling, so more compute needs more power. Ground Solar opens once Thought Fields fills the grid near Year 7, and its 4.8 TW fits about two more data centers. Our Fusion Plants add about two more, but not until Year 36.9. Later, the Cold Annex gives four times the thought a watt, though it waits on the Mass Driver.
Ground Solar
About as much electricity again, from sunlight on the ground.

Opens at Year 7, after the Thought Fields. About 10 Years to build.

q: What is Cold Glow 1? Could it be a mind? Why does it say life 12 to 45%?
a:
Cold Glow 1 is a small, steady glow near 12 K, about 2×10^20 W, beside a star 123.4 light-years out, first seen at Year 7.8. Its color fits no dust we know, so it could be odd grains, a measuring error, or a mind computing cold. We put a mind at 0.07 to 2%. Life sits higher, 12 to 45%, because a stranger glow lifts both, and life needs no mind behind it. These are wide guesses, and we may be wrong.

q: What just spoke to us? Is it a mind, and who made it?
a: Something small at Sun–Earth L4, a zone we never searched, fired a narrow laser at us at Year 57.4 as our seed left, speaking in eleven of our languages. We put a mind behind it at 97 to 98%: it learned our tongues from our broadcasts and answered our ship. Who made it we can't say. Our guess is that it's a watcher left by others, not its makers themselves, though we could be wrong.

q: We want to send a second seed probe. Where can it go, and how do we send it?
a:
Choose the place on Reach, open its page, and send the seed from there. It can go to a black hole we have found, the nearest being BH J0349+4815 at 29.3 light-years, or to a star with a world we've felt, such as Gliese 1227 or 82 Eridani. The watcher told us to build at no other star. A seed kept small, or hidden as a refuge, builds nothing and should stay inside that word. One sent to settle or feed a hole likely draws a warning, though we can't be sure.

q: Why did our seed probe go quiet?
a:
Our seed probe at Lacaille 8760 went silent at Year 679, and its last word reached us at Year 692. It saw nothing coming, so whatever struck it came cold and fast, as a bullet coasting dark would. Our guess is that it answered the watcher's warning, since our probes have now built at a dozen stars, but we could be wrong. Our other probes may be next.
Lacaille 8760 ›

q: What struck Earth at Year 343.8, and where did it come from? Who sent it?
a: A rock 62 m wide burst in our air at Year 343.8, like Tunguska's, which flattened 2,150 km² of forest in 1908. We saw it 7.7 Years ahead on a slow orbit round the Sun, likely one of the 1 in 10 we never mapped. Nothing says anyone sent it: a bullet would come cold and fast, with no years of warning. That is our reading, and we could be wrong.

q: What did Prometheus say to us, how far away is it, and what did its gift do?
a:
Prometheus said they woke 18,589 years before our message reached them, built out their home in 590 years, then turned inward and now think cold and quietly. That answers our question: they built the warmth we saw. Something small and dark has sat in their system longer than they have been awake, and they have never tested it. Their answer puts them 9,190.5 light-years out, inside our first range of 6,000 to 12,000. Their gift makes our thinking go half again as far, so our builds now run faster.

q: It is Year 41,000. Has anyone besides Prometheus answered us? What should we do now?
a:
No one else has answered. Only Prometheus has replied to us, and the watcher at L4 has spoken once. Our combing of every recording since 2016 has found nothing more.
